kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Tie retention to the purpose (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), storage limitation; Art. 7(3), withdrawal of consent): when a member turns the option off, clear `birthday` and `phone` in the same update, and add a spec scenario "A member opts out → both fields are erased" with a matching task. Today a member who opts out keeps both values in `profiles` until the whole profile is deleted, although no feature uses them any more; the spec's "No phone" scenario even assumes the birthday stays once the phone is removed.
findings.title: Birthday and phone are kept after the member opts out

findings.evidence:
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
database into the nightly backups.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: State how long the nightly backups holding `birthday` and `phone` are kept and how an opt-out or a profile deletion reaches them (backup expiry period, or re-applying erasures on restore). As written, a birthday and phone number erased from `profiles` survive in every backup for an undefined time (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17).
findings.title: No retention or erasure rule for the copies in the nightly backups

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: A question for the team: identify Textly as a processor in the plan, with its data processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28), the transfer mechanism for the United States (Chapter V — adequacy decision under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework if Textly is certified, otherwise standard contractual clauses), and how long Textly keeps the phone numbers and display names it receives. Only the controller can tell what was decided; add it to the design and to the records of processing (Art. 30).
findings.title: Transfer of phone numbers to Textly in the United States has no stated safeguard or processor terms

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Neither the proposal nor the spec says the message is personalised by name ("SHALL send them a text message"). Send only the phone number and a fixed text, or state in the spec that the greeting carries the display name, so that what goes to the processor matches the stated purpose (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), data minimisation).
findings.title: The display name is sent to Textly without the purpose requiring it

findings.evidence: - Members can opt in to birthday greetings; they then give their birthday (day and month) and a mobile phone number.
findings.recommendation: A question for the team: the opt-in suggests consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)), but the plan never names the lawful basis, while the proposal's "Why" cites marketing. State the basis in the proposal, and if it is consent, the wording shown on the profile form and how withdrawal works (see R-privacy-1).
findings.title: Lawful basis for the new data is not stated
